The Partial Autocorrelation Function (PACF) is a diagnostic tool in time series analysis (specifically the Box-Jenkins method) used to identify the order of an autoregressive (AR) model. In contrast, the Autocorrelation Function (ACF) is typically used to identify the order of a moving average (MA) model.

In this context, a PACF that cuts off (drops to zero) at lag $p$ indicates an AR($p$) process, while a PACF that tails off suggests an MA or ARMA process. Therefore, the PACF is the specific diagnostic used to distinguish an AR process from an MA process (where the PACF exhibits the opposite tailing behavior). While it can also help differentiate specific AR components within ARIMA structures, the fundamental distinction usually taught is between the pure AR and pure MA models based on these cutoffs.

    *   For MA(q) models, ACF cuts off (becomes zero after lag q).
